stdout: package: @astryxdesign/lab # DialogHeroHeader Drop into Layout's header slot inside a Dialog, exactly like DialogHeader. Use when the dialog opens onto a featured, marketing, or onboarding moment where the compact DialogHeader is too understated. The media bleeds to the dialog's edges automatically and the close button floats over its top-trailing corner. The visible title is the default initial focus target; inline previews do not move focus. Install @astryxdesign/lab@canary with @astryxdesign/core@canary and import both packages’ CSS. Lab APIs can change between canary versions. **Import:** `import {DialogHeroHeader} from '@astryxdesign/lab';` ## Best Practices - **Do:** Set mediaMode to match the media's luminance so the overlaid close button stays legible: dark imagery needs mediaMode="dark". - **Do:** Size the media content to fill the slot (width 100% for images); the slot itself only positions and bleeds. - **Do:** Keep actions (CTAs) in LayoutFooter; the hero header takes no actions slot. - **Do:** Use isTitleHidden when the media already communicates the message visually; the title still names the dialog for screen readers. - **Don't:** Use for routine confirmations or forms; use the compact DialogHeader instead. - **Don't:** Pass decorative media without an empty alt: use alt="" on purely decorative images so screen readers skip them. ## Props | Prop | Type | Default | Description | |------|------|---------|-------------| | `title` | `string \| ReactElement` | - | Dialog title. A string is wrapped in a level 2 Heading (matching DialogHeader); pass a pre-styled Heading element to customize the treatment. Provides the accessible label for the parent Dialog via aria-labelledby unless the Dialog has an explicit label. The visible title is the default initial focus target; another eligible descendant autofocus request takes priority. A custom Heading receives the label and focus on its own element; if it sets its own id, name the Dialog with aria-labelledby. **(required)** | | `media` | `ReactNode` | - | Full-bleed visual rendered above the title (image, illustration, or icon). Stretches to the dialog's padded edges; the close button overlays its top-trailing corner. Size the media itself (e.g. width 100%) to fill the slot. **(required)** | | `mediaMode` | `'light' \| 'dark'` | - | Luminance of the media surface. Composes MediaTheme under the hood so content overlaid on the media (the close button) picks up contrast-safe inverted tokens: 'dark' media gets light overlay content, 'light' media gets dark. Omit to keep ambient theme tokens. | | `isTitleHidden` | `boolean` | `false` | Visually hides the title row while keeping it available to screen readers, so the dialog stays named by the title. | | `startContent` | `ReactNode` | - | Content placed before the title (e.g. an icon), inline with the heading. | | `maxLines` | `number` | - | Max lines before the title truncates with an ellipsis. Only applies when title is a string (auto-wrapped in a Heading). | | `onOpenChange` | `(isOpen: boolean) => unknown` | - | Close button callback, called with false when the close button is clicked. If not provided, no close button is rendered. Same contract as DialogHeader. | | `hasDivider` | `boolean` | - | Adds a themed border at the bottom edge. Defaults to the parent Layout's defaultHasDividers context value. | ## Examples ### Onboarding dialog ```tsx import {DialogHeroHeader} from '@astryxdesign/lab'; import '@astryxdesign/core/astryx.css'; import '@astryxdesign/lab/lab.css'; const [isOpen, setIsOpen] = useState(true); } mediaMode="dark" onOpenChange={setIsOpen} /> } content={Get started in three steps.} footer={ ``` ### Hidden title (media carries the message) ```tsx } isTitleHidden onOpenChange={setIsOpen} /> ```
